subsections.subsection_title: 11.1 Causes and Risk Factors of Cancer

Obesity, processed meat, aflatoxin and poor dietary patterns
Chronic hepatitis, inflammatory bowel disease, chronic gastritis
Early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity in certain cancers
HPV, HBV, HCV, EBV, HIV, H. pylori

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Cancer development is usually multifactorial, involving genetic alterations, environmental exposures and interactions between host and lifestyle factors.
This is one of the most important cancer warning-sign mnemonics.

rows: Change in bowel or bladder habits
A sore that does not heal
Cervical, endometrial, colorectal or urinary cancer
Breast, testicular or other soft-tissue malignancy
Obvious change in a wart or mole

blocks.text: A 55-year-old patient presents with progressive dysphagia and unexplained weight loss.
Think of oesophageal or gastric malignancy and arrange urgent assessment.
Exam pearl: CAUTION is a symptom-recognition mnemonic, not a diagnostic criterion. Many patients with cancer do not present with these symptoms.

Paraneoplastic syndromes are clinical manifestations caused by malignancy through hormonal secretion, immune cross-reactivity or other tumour-mediated mechanisms, rather than direct tumour invasion or metastasis.

items.text: AFP = A for liver and germ-cell tumours.
Supporting diagnosis in appropriate clinical settings.

blocks.text: They are not generally sufficiently sensitive or specific to be used alone for cancer diagnosis or population screening.
Exam pearl: AFP is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma, but AFP can also rise in pregnancy and certain germ-cell tumours.
Cancer staging describes the anatomical extent of malignancy.

items.text: T0: No evidence of primary tumour.
T1–T4: Increasing tumour size or local extent, depending on cancer type.
N0: No regional lymph node involvement.
N1–N3: Increasing extent of regional lymph node involvement.
Staging tells you how far the cancer has spread.
Staging helps determine treatment and prognosis.
TNM is not applied identically to every malignancy; some cancers have their own staging systems.

blocks.text: Cancer grading describes how abnormal tumour cells appear and how closely they resemble their normal tissue of origin.
Exam pearl: A small, poorly differentiated tumour can be high grade but low stage.
Cancer cachexia is a multifactorial syndrome characterised by ongoing skeletal muscle loss, with or without loss of fat mass, that cannot be fully reversed by conventional nutritional support.

rows: Cytokine release, especially IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-α

items.text: Increased energy expenditure and systemic inflammation.
Increased protein and fat breakdown with impaired anabolic metabolism.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Cancer cachexia is not simply starvation. Nutritional supplementation alone may not reverse it because of the underlying metabolic and inflammatory abnormalities.

rows: Yellowing of skin from hepatic injury (jaundice)

blocks.text: Exam pearl: A patient receiving chemotherapy who develops fever and neutropenia should be treated as having a potential oncological emergency.
Additional complications according to the irradiated region

items.text: Acute effects: During treatment or shortly afterwards.
Subacute effects: Weeks to months later.
Late effects: Months to years later.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Radiation effects are generally most pronounced in tissues with rapidly dividing cells, although late injury can affect many normal tissues.
This is a high-yield framework for recognising life-threatening complications in patients with malignancy.

rows: Back pain, weakness, sensory loss, sphincter dysfunction
Hypotension, raised JVP, muffled heart sounds
Severe metabolic disturbance in selected malignancies
Bleeding from tumour invasion or thrombocytopenia

items.text: Involve oncology and relevant specialist teams.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Do not delay antibiotics in suspected neutropenic sepsis while waiting for investigations.

subsections.subsection_title: 11.11 Causes of Superior Vena Cava Syndrome

blocks.text: Superior vena cava syndrome results from obstruction of blood flow through the superior vena cava.

| Cause | Explanation |

| S | Small-cell lung carcinoma | Common malignant cause |
| C | Central venous catheter thrombosis | Catheter-associated obstruction |
| C | Clots/thrombosis | SVC thrombosis |
| C | Chronic mediastinal fibrosis | Fibrosing mediastinitis |
| M | Mediastinal lymphoma | Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma |
| C | Other lung cancers | Especially non-small-cell lung cancer |
| C | Compression by mediastinal masses | Thymoma, germ-cell tumours and other masses |
Exam pearl: The classic association is lung cancer, particularly small-cell lung carcinoma, although lymphoma and benign thrombotic causes are also important.
Tumour lysis syndrome occurs when large numbers of malignant cells break down rapidly, releasing intracellular contents into the circulation.

rows: Oncological treatment causing rapid tumour destruction

items.text: Other rapidly proliferating or highly treatment-sensitive malignancies.
F – Fluids: Adequate IV hydration, with careful monitoring.
L – Laboratory monitoring: Serial electrolytes, uric acid and renal function.
U – Urate reduction: Allopurinol or rasburicase according to risk and clinical circumstances.
I – Identify and correct electrolyte disturbances.
S – Specialist involvement and close monitoring.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: Rasburicase rapidly converts uric acid into allantoin. It is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency because of the risk of haemolysis and methemoglobinaemia.
Spinal cord compression is an oncological emergency, particularly when caused by metastatic disease.

rows: Breast, lung, prostate, renal and thyroid cancers

blocks.text: Important primary malignancies that metastasise to the spine
Other causes include lymphoma and multiple myeloma.

items.text: B – Back pain, often progressive or worse at night.
A – Altered sensation and sensory level.
C – Cord dysfunction with limb weakness.
K – Kidney/bladder and bowel dysfunction, including urinary retention or incontinence.
Saddle sensory changes in relevant lower spinal lesions.
Urgent MRI of the whole spine.
Immobilisation or spinal precautions where indicated.
Prompt dexamethasone when malignant spinal cord compression is suspected, following local protocol.
Urgent oncology and spinal surgical assessment.
Radiotherapy, surgery or both, depending on the clinical situation.

blocks.text: Exam pearl: New severe back pain in a patient with known cancer should raise suspicion for metastatic spinal disease, even before neurological deficits develop.
